TL;DR: How much can we stop duplicating effort and instead build shared tools for verifying Rust code?

Response requested on these concrete asks:

  • What is everyone's availability for a meeting either tomorrow (Fri May 1) or some time next week?
  • Which of the following would you have use for? Which would you contribute to? (see below for details)
    • Generic setup sub-command (cargo hax setup, cargo anneal setup, etc)
    • Library to programmatically drive Charon/Aeneas
    • Library to programmatically drive Lean/Lake
    • Improvements to Lean/Lake itself to support being driven programmatically, and to support being run in parallel

Hey folks!

Seems like there are a lot of different people/teams/projects who are duplicating effort where we could instead be sharing resources/building shared tools. I've already talked to the Hax developers (@Clément Blaudeau, @Maxime Buyse, and @Karthikeyan Bhargavan) and to the Annodized developer (@Mate Kovacs) about the idea of sharing infrastructure and code. I'd like to see who else would be interested in participating.

"Sharing" here may mean different things in different instances:

  • Maintaining libraries distributed on crates.io
  • Maintaining GitHub Actions distributed on GitHub
  • Defining standard configuration file formats
  • Hosting shared infrastructure (e.g., shared GitHub repos for this code to live in)

Here are all of the things that folks might be interested in sharing.

setup sub-command

For anyone using Charon/Aeneas/Lean, building entirely from source may require some or all of Rust, Cargo, OCaml, Opam, Dune, Elan, Lean, and Lake. Asking users to build deps from source is a barrier to adoption.

Anneal provides a cargo anneal setup sub-command which automatically downloads pre-built artifacts for Charon and Aeneas, and pre-builds some Lean artifacts that can later be re-used. Shared setup command support would likely entail:

  • A configuration file format for specifying dependencies and how to build them from source
  • A GitHub Action that consumes this configuration file, builds dependencies, and publishes them to GitHub's artifact hosting
  • A Rust crate that consumes this configuration file, downloads/installs these pre-built artifacts from GitHub, and optionally runs other local commands (e.g. to support what cannot be pre-built, or to support hooking into existing toolchain dependency tools like rustup or elan)

Programmatically driving Charon and Aeneas

A lot of our projects use Charon to go from .rs to .llbc and Aeneas to go from .llbc to .lean. Both accept a wide range of flags and require a good amount of scaffolding to be used correctly. Shared support for this would look like:

  • Building on the setup command support described above to distribute pre-built binaries of Charon and Aeneas, maybe pre-built .olean files of Aeneas's Lean library, and maybe other pre-built artifacts
  • A Rust crate that supports all of our use cases, presumably via configuration options, and drives Charon and Aeneas to produce Lean programs

Programmatically driving Lean

The previous section's library could be extended to support Lean/Lake as well. This is a bit different because needs may differ more from project to project. For Anneal, our primary concern is being able to pre-build binary artifacts (e.g., .olean files) and then re-use these in each invocation of lake build. Lake is not designed for this use case, and so we've found that it requires a lot of scaffolding and a lot of holding Lake very carefully to get this working (i.e. to ensure that Lake neither re-builds unnecessarily nor races with other Lake processes in making filesystem modifications).

Improvements to Lean/Lake to support being driven programmatically and in parallel

See the previous section – we may also be able to upstream improvements that make this easier.

Thanks for joining, everyone! My own manual notes:

Notes

  • Agenda
    • Derek – Ponky3Verif
      • Project is being actively developed (3 commits in the past few hours)
      • Need to be able to have verification stay up to date with rapid pace of development
      • Goal: In each crate, have a proof directory w/ extractions
        • All of the proofs “import each other”
  • Tools
    • For all of this, compatibility with cargo, cargo flags, etc
      • E.g., ability to enforce specs via proof vs as runtime checks
    • Setup management
      • Installs binary dependencies
      • Checks that current installation is valid
      • Permits shelling out to non-managed binaries
      • Needs CI infrastructure to build/publish pre-builts (binaries and object files (e.g. .olean))
      • Needs hosting infrastructure (currently mostly uses GitHub)
      • Needs the ability to pin to specific versions + verify hashes
      • Needs the ability to run complex setup “scripts”
      • Needs the ability to do various filesystem muckery
      • Should ideally support declarative configuration
        • This configures:
          • What is built/published in CI
          • What is installed on user’s machine
        • On CI, requires computing every possible configuration
        • On the user’s machine, computing every possible configuration that you could request at “verify time”
  • Toolchain orchestration (Charon, Aeneas, Lean/Lake)
    • Provides feedback from this orchestration
    • Emits “TCB audit log”
      • Includes anything in your TCB – toolchains, axioms, hardware behavior, etc
    • Provides timing information
      • Performance information about how long each tool invocation takes
      • Timings for individual Lean proofs?
      • Prior art: Lean’s Radar tool
  • Lean libraries (e.g., formalization of Rust opsem)
  • Something related to monorepo-ing things? Like “auto-bump”?
  • Clément: More foundational questons about which Lean frameworks are being used (e.g., mvcgen?)
  • Alex/Derek: Bumping Mathlib can be painful. Support for pinning various tools and their corresponding toolchains would be nice.
  • Jonathan: How much can Nix help here? Charon/Aeneas use Nix everywhere and it helps a lot.
  • Lifecycle of cargo anneal verify:
    • cargo install … -> Produces cargo-anneal binary
    • cargo anneal setup
      • Download pre-builts (either hosted ourselves or hosted by external parties)
        • For ones we built ourselves: Need CI infrastructure for building + hosting
      • Need CI infrastructure for rolling pinned dependencies
      • Run some scripts locally
        • Install elan
        • Use elan to install Lean
        • Run various Lean setup like lake exe cache get (ie, pre-downloads Mathlib, pre-builds Aeneas Lean library)
        • Various Git repo hackery
      • Hax: This rebuilds the “Hax engine” locally
        • Might want to prefer rebuilding from source vs downloading binaries
        • Requires OCaml toolchain
    • cargo anneal verify
      • Accept various Cargo flags to specify targets to verify (—example, —workspace, etc)
      • Resolve Cargo dependencies and parse .rs files
      • Invoke Charon to lower everything to .llbc, figuring out environment variables and flags to pass
        • In Anneal’s case, env vars specify where the Rust toolchain components are installed (in ~/.anneal/toolchains/…)
          • Hax: Assumes globally-installed toolchains; doesn’t manage its own (no equivalent ~/.hax)
      • Invoke Aeneas, passing .llbc, producing .lean
      • Write or modify our own lakefile.toml or lakefile.lean files, configuring these to “hook up” to what was installed via cargo anneal setup
      • Invoke lake build
        • Hax: Currently doesn’t drive Lean/Lake
      • Hax: Supports multiple backends, so you could do cargo hax-into-lean, cargo hax-into-fstar, etc
      • Rewrite any errors/diagnostics to be user-understandable
  • Clément: Need to think about how the feedback we produce can be machine-readable and consumed by various other tools
    • E.g., need source maps
    • Fun questions: Can we make this incremental? How much can we cache w/o worrying about stale caches? Etc
  • Josh: Emilio has a demo of Lean goodies in .rs files
